phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: CRITICAL FINDING: validateWithKzgBatchVerifier creates an unbuffered channel resChan := make(chan error) and sends it to kzgChan. The kzgVerifierRoutine processes the batch and attempts to send the result back via verifier.resChan <- verificationErr. However, if the caller's context expires (slot timeout = SecondsPerSlot) before the batch result is ready, the caller exits its select block and stops reading from resChan. Since resChan is unbuffered, the kzgVerifierRoutine BLOCKS permanently on the send operation. This blocks the single kzgVerifierRoutine goroutine, halting all subsequent KZG verification for the node.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: deduplicate_commitments in eip7594.c uses commitments_equal (48-byte memcmp) for deduplication. Security question: can two distinct 48-byte sequences represent the same BLS12-381 G1 point? In BLS12-381 compressed format (used by ETH2 and enforced by blst), each valid G1 point has exactly one canonical byte representation. The infinity point has a specific encoding. blst's blst_p1_uncompress rejects non-canonical encodings. Therefore, byte equality is equivalent to semantic equality for all valid curve points that pass the parsing step.
state_anomalies_found: BLS12-381 compressed G1 has unique canonical encoding enforced by blst
deduplicate_commitments operates on raw bytes before point parsing -- but non-canonical bytes would be rejected at parsing time later
No non-canonical commitment representation can both pass parsing and be deduplicated differently from its canonical form

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Non-canonical commitment attack: attacker sends Bytes48 values that represent the same G1 point but with different bytes. BLS12-381 compressed format does not admit multiple encodings for the same point (the x-coordinate plus compression bit is unique). blst enforces this. Additionally, the C library calls bytes_to_bls_one_g1 (or equivalent) which rejects non-canonical points with C_KZG_BADARGS.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Integrated analysis of batch KZG verification security across CHK-0108 through CHK-0114. Primary confirmed vulnerability: unbuffered resChan deadlock (CHK-0109). Secondary informational: batch poisoning DoS (CHK-0108). All cryptographic invariants (RLC soundness CHK-0113, commitment deduplication CHK-0114) are sound. All input validation invariants (bounds CHK-0101 through 0103, length CHK-0104 through 0107) are correct. The dominant actionable finding is the unbuffered channel deadlock.
state_anomalies_found: CONFIRMED: resChan := make(chan error) (unbuffered) in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier causes kzgVerifierRoutine deadlock on context timeout (batch_verifier.go:163)
INFORMATIONAL: batch poisoning forces fallback to individual verification
SOUND: cell_index bounds (NumberOfColumns==CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB==128)
SOUND: equal-length arrays (loop construction guarantee)
SOUND: RLC challenge (Blake2b hash of all inputs)
SOUND: commitment deduplication (BLS12-381 canonical encoding)
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: Overall: KZG verification state management correct except unbuffered channel.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: kzgVerifierRoutine single-goroutine model correct except for unbuffered resChan deadlock vulnerability.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Primary exploit (CHK-0109 confirmed): cause validation to take >12 seconds (SecondsPerSlot) via slow parent state lookup. ctx.Done() fires in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier. Caller returns ValidationIgnore. kzgVerifierRoutine permanently blocks at verifier.resChan <- verificationErr (batch_verifier.go:211). All subsequent KZG verifications halt. The fix is make(chan error, 1).
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: CONFIRMED: Unbuffered resChan deadlock in kzgVerifierRoutine. Trigger: SecondsPerSlot timeout in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier. Effect: permanent halt of KZG verification service. Fix: make(chan error, 1) at batch_verifier.go:163.
attack_scenarios: Primary (active): slow parent state lookup + high KZG load -> SecondsPerSlot timeout -> kzgVerifierRoutine deadlock
Secondary (passive): high network load -> natural timeouts -> deadlock without attacker involvement
Tertiary: batch poisoning DoS -> fallback amplification
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Primary: requires >12s batch processing. Achievable under load or with crafted slow-validation inputs.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Primary vulnerability (CHK-0109) is externally triggerable from P2P. Effect: permanent halt of data column sidecar KZG verification.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: P2P gossip: craft DataColumnSidecar with slow-validation parent block, trigger SecondsPerSlot timeout, deadlock kzgVerifierRoutine.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Critical invariant fails: kzgVerifierRoutine can be permanently stalled by an unbuffered resChan send to a timed-out receiver. All other security and correctness invariants hold. The single fix (make(chan error, 1)) restores all invariants.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: INSUFFICIENT: current make(chan error) is unbuffered. Must be make(chan error, 1).
edge_cases: With make(chan error, 1): verifyKzgBatch always completes immediately without blocking; timed-out callers ignore the buffered result; service shutdown cleanly terminates kzgVerifierRoutine
Concurrent timeouts: with buffered channels, each timed-out request results in one unread buffered error (garbage collected); kzgVerifierRoutine continues processing

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: CONFIRMED HIGH-SEVERITY DoS VULNERABILITY: unbuffered resChan in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier (batch_verifier.go:163) combined with SecondsPerSlot context timeout creates a permanently-deadlocking condition in kzgVerifierRoutine. Externally triggerable from P2P by causing slow validation. Effect: all data column sidecar KZG verification halted until node restart. Under natural high-load conditions, this can occur without attacker involvement.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: CRITICAL FIX (batch_verifier.go line 163): Change resChan := make(chan error) to resChan := make(chan error, 1). This is a one-line fix that eliminates the deadlock by ensuring verifyKzgBatch can always complete its send operation without blocking on a timed-out receiver.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.severity_estimate: High (DoS - permanently halts KZG verification service, externally triggerable)
